chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The penalty is not established upon the istihada (continuous menstruation) woman until the blood ceases from her.

key_terms.الْحَدُّ: The fixed legal penalty prescribed in Islamic law
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: A woman suffering from istihada (irregular/continuous menstruation)

ai.seo_question: When is the hadd penalty not applied to a woman with istihada?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the fixed legal penalty (hadd) is suspended for a woman with istihada (irregular bleeding) until the bleeding ceases, distinguishing her status from that of a regular menstruating woman. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly principle that istihada does not carry the same ritual impurity restrictions as hayd, thereby affecting the applicability of specific legal penalties during the period of continuous flow.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Penalty would not be established upon the menstruating woman until the (flow of) blood is cut off from her’.
